original_question: Can one solve enumeration problems for restricted classes of parking functions on rooted trees or on mappings, rather than only for the unrestricted parking functions considered in the existing counting results?
target_in_paper: Section 3, open-problems list inherited from Lackner and Panholzer, item (6): "One could consider enumeration problems for some restricted parking functions for trees (or mappings)." The same direction is restated in Section 5.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the relevant open direction as an enumeration problem for restricted parking functions, and it correctly keeps the scope on trees/mappings rather than drifting to neighboring open problems such as other tree families, displacements, defective parking functions, or scaling limits.
missing_details: The paper works with rooted labelled trees T on [n] and n-mappings f:[n]->[n], not arbitrary rooted trees or general digraphs.
The surrounding counting results are total counts of successful pairs (T,s) and (f,s), where s in [n]^m is a parking function; the draft does not state this pair-counting setup.
The existing unrestricted counts in context are the total numbers F_{n,m} and M_{n,m} of tree and mapping parking functions, respectively; the draft does not identify that benchmark explicitly.

The paper does not specify any particular restricted subclass. To stay faithful, the refined question must leave the restricted class abstract (or chosen in advance), rather than inventing a concrete family not singled out in the paper.

In this setting, a parking function means that each driver starts at its preferred vertex and follows the directed edges toward the root / along the functional digraph until reaching the first vacant parking place, and all drivers succeed; the draft leaves this implicit.
This is an open problem/direction, not a theorem, conjecture with fixed hypotheses, or an equivalence statement.
No ambient ring, field, operator, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are part of this problem; it is purely combinatorial.
refined_question: For rooted labelled trees T on [n] (with edges oriented toward the root) and n-mappings f:[n]->[n] viewed through their functional digraphs, a sequence s in [n]^m is a parking function if each driver, starting at its preferred vertex and then following the directed edges until the first vacant vertex, eventually parks. Beyond the unrestricted total counts F_{n,m} and M_{n,m} of all successful pairs (T,s) and (f,s), can one obtain analogous exact or asymptotic enumeration results for a specified nontrivial restricted subclass of tree or mapping parking functions?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact open problem stated in Section 3, item (6). The nearby Section 3 context makes clear that the baseline results being contrasted with are the total enumerations of unrestricted tree and mapping parking functions, first for the m=n case and then for general m, counted as pairs (T,s) and (f,s). Section 5 restates the same direction almost verbatim. Because the paper itself does not choose or define a specific restricted family, the sharpest faithful rewrite is to parameterize the restriction by a chosen subclass rather than narrowing to a new example not singled out in the survey.
